title: TIDELINE
logline: A harbour watchkeeper finds a broken railing at dawn and races the tide to search for whoever went over, against official delay and a colleague who already knows what the sea keeps.
premise: Maren Vosk, a harbour-station watchkeeper in her fifties, finds the east-wall railing bent outward and the paint still wet. Coastguard cannot launch for four hours — the whole tide — so she takes the station boat herself, with Derek Algood riding along to tell her it is not a search. On a sandbar nobody stands on twice she finds a shoe, photographs it, and puts it back. That night she files the photograph and the shoe in a fifth identical box while Derek sleeps in the chair. Insisting a missing person is still searchable does not bring them back; it only adds another box to the shelf.

audience.reader_promise: The cost of a search that cannot succeed, paid in a fifth box and a colleague who will not make her sleep.

places: launch boat at the harbour mouth
rules_of_the_world: Tides run on a clock no one can delay; four hours is a full tide and closes a search window.
Coastguard cannot put a boat out in under four hours.
Wet paint on a bent railing is treated as a reliable stamp that someone went over.
The sandbar at low water is ground nobody stands on twice.
The station boat can be taken with a board key; procedure does not physically stop them.
The station keeps unofficial physical archives the official search will not.
The missing person is not returned inside this day; only objects come back.
The sea is indifferent; nothing supernatural answers a torch.

prose_touchstones: Kelly Reichardt (Wendy and Lucy) — spare working observation, feeling carried by objects
Hemingway iceberg — short declarative action, dialogue that refuses to name the wound
No Country for Old Men action-line economy
forbidden_tics: we see or other camera-directing beyond CUT TO
Derek as villain or sudden convert
music or score cues used as emotion

action_adventure.evidence: They launch across a white line of broken water at the bar.

crime.evidence: An unofficial evidence bag and a possible going-over; no crime is proved.

detective.evidence: Maren times the fall, walks the bar, photographs a shoe, and files it.

drama.evidence: The spine is Maren’s will against tide, procedure, and Derek; remove it and nothing remains.

gothic.evidence: Pre-dawn sodium lamp, a sandbar nobody walks twice, a shelf of prior losses.

mystery.evidence: Wet paint, time of entry, and a shoe cue the audience; no culprit is unmasked.

thriller.evidence: Four hours is the whole tide; they must launch themselves or lose the bar.

tragedy.evidence: The person is already gone; her compulsion only adds a fifth box.

arousal.evidence: Pre-dawn wall and a boat over the bar, then a still night office.

bittersweetness.evidence: Photographing a shoe and shelving it is tenderness inside loss.

character_complexity.evidence: Maren’s sleepless protocol and four prior boxes; Derek’s reasonable care. Mixed motives.

cliffhanger_frequency.evidence: Empty water, the taken key, the wheel into the bar, the fifth box.

conflict_density.evidence: Every scene is insistence versus resistance: delay, launch, bar, shelf.

diversity_representation.evidence: Older woman lead, younger male colleague; no further identity work.

emotional_depth.evidence: Nightdress, wet boots, I sleep / You don’t, and the boxes carry feeling.

emotional_range.evidence: Stubborn duty, weary care, and quiet grief; no other registers.

empathy_elicitation.evidence: Nightdress under waterproofs, wet boots, Derek asleep still arguing: both sides land.

moral_ambiguity.evidence: Derek is right it is not a search; Maren is right to go anyway.

mystery_complexity.evidence: Wet paint, time of entry, and a shoe; no reveal recontextualises them.

narrative_complexity.evidence: One linear day; the four prior boxes add a single retrospective layer.

pacing_intensity.evidence: Five causal scenes in one day; the night scene stops rather than cascades.

philosophical_depth.evidence: What is owed the missing once the tide has already taken them.

relationship_centrality.evidence: Maren and Derek’s insistence-versus-resistance drives office, boat, and night.

suspense_threat.evidence: A four-hour tide clock and broken water; the person is already gone.

symbolism_allegory.evidence: Tide erases; identical boxes stack failed searches; the shoe is replaced exactly.

valence.evidence: Night coda files a shoe in a fifth identical box; nobody is found.

violence_level.evidence: A bent railing and an implied drowning; no blow is shown.

worldbuilding_detail.evidence: Tide charts in three hands, key board, sandbar rule, unofficial boxes.

must_include: bent east-wall railing with wet paint before dawn
four-hour coastguard delay named as the whole tide

naming or identifying who went over
Derek as villain or last-minute convert

score or music cues as emotion

keep_in_mind: Core conflict: Maren insists the person is still searchable; the tide, the four-hour coastguard clock, and Derek insist the search is already over.
Crucible: both are bound to the harbour station and to each other by the watch; she cannot leave a wet railing unfollowed, and he cannot let her take the bar alone.
Premise to prove: insisting the missing are still searchable does not recover them; it only adds another box.
Derek’s motive is human and sympathisable — he knows the tide and is trying to keep her from another night she will not sleep.
Never identify who went over. Never show a body. Never let Coastguard arrive in time.
Externalise everything: wet paint on fingers, wet boots, key off the board, shoe replaced exactly, fifth box on the shelf.
Subtext only. Banned: stating the theme, naming grief, explaining the four prior boxes, as-you-know procedure talk.
Conflict rises one step per scene: report, official delay, unsanctioned launch, crossing the bar, the shoe, the shelf of boxes.
Maren operates at maximum capacity inside her competence (charts, boat, evidence protocol); taking the bar is will, not idiocy.
The nightdress under waterproofs and the four identical boxes are plants that fire without commentary.
Enter late, leave early. No scene exists to brief the audience on how a harbour station works.
Equalise forces: Derek is not a blocker to be overridden; he is right that it is not a search, and the story must let him be right.
One plot. No romance, no comic foil, no secondary case.
Dialogue stays short, functional, and slightly behind the feeling. Parentheticals only for address (radio, to herself, eyes closed).
The sandbar rule — nobody stands on it twice — is a world constraint, not a metaphor to be spoken.
